questions.answer: Start with \(\begin{pmatrix}1&1&5\\1&-1&1\end{pmatrix}\). Use \(\mathbb R^2\) <- \(\mathbb R^2\) - \(\mathbb R^1\) to get \(\begin{pmatrix}1&1&5\\0&-2&-4\end{pmatrix}\). Scale \(\mathbb R^2\) by -1/2 to get \(\begin{pmatrix}1&1&5\\0&1&2\end{pmatrix}\). Eliminate above the second pivot using \(\mathbb R^1\) <- \(\mathbb R^1\) - \(\mathbb R^2\), giving \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&3\\0&1&2\end{pmatrix}\). Therefore \(x=3\) and \(y=2\).

Scale \(\mathbb R^1\) by 1/2 to get \((1,0,3)\). Scale \(\mathbb R^2\) by 1/5 to get \((0,1,2)\). The matrix is then \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&3\\0&1&2\end{pmatrix}\), which is already reduced. Therefore \(x=3\) and \(y=2\).

Use \(\mathbb R^2\) <- \(\mathbb R^2\) - 3R1 to get \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2&7\\0&-2&-4\end{pmatrix}\). Scale \(\mathbb R^2\) by -1/2 to get \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2&7\\0&1&2\end{pmatrix}\). Use \(\mathbb R^1\) <- \(\mathbb R^1\) - 2R2 to get \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&3\\0&1&2\end{pmatrix}\). Therefore \(x=3\) and \(y=2\).

Start from the bottom pivot. Row 3 gives \(z=2\). Eliminate z from row 2 using \(\mathbb R^2\) <- \(\mathbb R^2\) + \(\mathbb R^3\), giving \((0,1,0,2)\). Eliminate z from row 1 using \(\mathbb R^1\) <- \(\mathbb R^1\) - \(\mathbb R^3\), giving \((1,1,0,4)\). Eliminate y from row 1 using \(\mathbb R^1\) <- \(\mathbb R^1\) - \(\mathbb R^2\), giving \((1,0,0,2)\). The RREF is \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0&2\\0&1&0&2\\0&0&1&2\end{pmatrix}\), so \((x, y, z)\) = \((2, 2, 2)\).

questions.prompt: Use Gauss-Jordan elimination to determine whether \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\2&4&7\end{pmatrix}\) is consistent.
questions.answer: Use \(\mathbb R^2\) <- \(\mathbb R^2\) - 2R1. The second row becomes \((2,4,7)\) - 2\((1,2,3)\) = \((0,0,1)\). This row represents 0x + 0y = 1, which is impossible. Therefore the system is inconsistent and has no solution.

questions.prompt: Use Gauss-Jordan elimination on \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\2&4&0\end{pmatrix}\) and describe the solutions.
questions.answer: Use \(\mathbb R^2\) <- \(\mathbb R^2\) - 2R1. The second row becomes \((0,0,0)\), so the matrix is \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}\). The first row says x + 2y = 0. Let \(y=t\). Then x = -2t. Therefore the solutions are \((x, y)\) = \((-2t, t)\), where t is any real number.

questions.prompt: Perform the first pivot step for \(\begin{pmatrix}0&1&2\\3&4&5\end{pmatrix}\) using Gauss-Jordan elimination.
questions.answer: A convenient first pivot should be non-zero in the first column. The first row has first entry 0, while the second row has first entry 3. Swap rows using \(\mathbb R^1\) <-> \(\mathbb R^2\). The matrix becomes \(\begin{pmatrix}3&4&5\\0&1&2\end{pmatrix}\). If desired, scale \(\mathbb R^1\) by 1/3 next to make the pivot equal to 1.

questions.prompt: Continue from \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2&5\\0&1&3\end{pmatrix}\) to RREF using Gauss-Jordan elimination.
questions.answer: The second pivot is already 1. To make the entry above it zero, use \(\mathbb R^1\) <- \(\mathbb R^1\) - 2R2. Compute \((1,2,5)\) - 2\((0,1,3)\) = \((1,0,-1)\). The RREF is \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&-1\\0&1&3\end{pmatrix}\). Therefore \(x=-1\) and \(y=3\).

Start with rows \(\mathbb R^1\) = \((1,-1,2,3)\), \(\mathbb R^2\) = \((2,1,-1,0)\), \(\mathbb R^3\) = \((1,1,1,6)\). Use \(\mathbb R^2\) <- \(\mathbb R^2\) - 2R1 to get \((0,3,-5,-6)\), and \(\mathbb R^3\) <- \(\mathbb R^3\) - \(\mathbb R^1\) to get \((0,2,-1,3)\). A shorter way is to solve the equations after elimination. From the original equations, subtract equation 1 from equation 3 to get 2y - \(z=3\). Subtract twice equation 1 from equation 2 to get 3y - 5z = -6. Solve these: multiply 2y - z = \(3\times 3\) to get 6y - 3z = 9, and multiply 3y - 5z = -\(6\times 2\) to get 6y - 10z = -12. Subtract to get 7z = 21, so \(z=3\). Then 2y - 3 = 3, so \(y=3\). Use x - y + 2z = 3: x - 3 + 6 = 3, so \(x=0\). The solution is \((0, 3, 3)\).

questions.prompt: A learner stops Gauss-Jordan elimination at \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2&5\\0&1&3\end{pmatrix}\) and reads \(x=5\), \(y=3\). Diagnose the error.
questions.answer: The matrix is in echelon form but not reduced row echelon form because there is a 2 above the pivot in column 2. The second row gives \(y=3\). The first row gives x + 2y = 5, not \(x=5\). Substituting \(y=3\) gives x + 6 = 5, so \(x=-1\). The learner read an echelon matrix as if it were already RREF.
